title: How to write a job posting for an electrician
summary: Paste your hiring notes into ChatGPT and get a plain job posting for an electrician. Check the pay, the license, and how to apply before you post it.

tests.prompt:
You help an electrical contractor write a job posting for an electrician. Draft only. Do not post it.

Fill in these details. If a line is blank, write UNKNOWN and do not guess.

Business name and town: [BUSINESS AND TOWN]
Job title: [JOB TITLE]
Work they will do: [DUTIES]
Experience you need: [EXPERIENCE]
License or certification needed: [LICENSE]
Pay range: [PAY]
Hours and days: [SCHEDULE]
Benefits or extras: [BENEFITS]
How to apply: [HOW TO APPLY]
What to include: [WHAT TO SEND]
Your name: [YOUR NAME]

Rules:
- Never invent details; if something is missing, ask or mark it UNKNOWN.
- Do not invent a pay number, a benefit, or a license requirement.
- Do not write "competitive pay" if [PAY] is blank. Mark PAY UNKNOWN instead.
- Keep it plain so an electrician can tell if they should apply.
- No buzzwords, no "ninja," and no "fast-paced environment."
- Write as the shop, not as a recruiter.

Output format:
Return these headings only:
Job title
Short intro (40 words or fewer)
The work
Who should apply
Pay and hours
Benefits
How to apply
Facts used
Unknown
Keep the full posting under 220 words.

setup.agent: Paste this into ChatGPT, or into the chat assistant you already use.
steps: Write the job title, the town, the work, the experience and license you need, the pay range, the hours, any benefits, and how to apply.
If pay or benefits are not decided, leave those lines blank instead of guessing.
Open ChatGPT, paste the ChatGPT prompt, and replace every [BRACKET]. Type UNKNOWN where you cannot fill a line.
Confirm the pay, the license, the hours, and the apply instructions. Delete anything you did not write down.
Copy the posting onto the board or site you use, and post it yourself.
setup.approvalStep: You check the pay, the license, and how to apply, then you post the ad yourself.
failureModes: The draft invents a pay range or a benefit. Put your real numbers back in.
The license line does not match what you legally need. Use the exact license.
The apply email or phone number is wrong or made up. Use only the method you provided.
The tone sounds like a corporate recruiter. Edit it back into plain shop language.

faq.q: Do I need to name the exact license?
faq.a: Yes, if you require one. Write the state or local license you actually need. A vague 'must be licensed' line wastes time for you and for applicants.

faq.q: Can I use this for an apprentice posting?
faq.a: Yes. Change the title, the duties, the experience, and the license line so they match an apprentice role. Do not leave journeyman language in the draft.

faq.q: Should I say how many trucks or how busy the shop is?
faq.a: Only if you want that in the ad and you typed it in the duties or extras. Do not let the draft invent a company size.

job: Paste hiring notes and get a plain job posting for an electrician.
who: Electrical shop owners who need to hire an electrician and want a clear ad without recruiter language.

example.scenario: A residential electrical shop needs a licensed electrician for service calls and panel work.
example.input:
Business name and town: Bright Path Electric, Midway
Job title: Licensed residential electrician
Work they will do: Service calls, panel upgrades, and lighting installs in homes
Experience you need: 4 years of residential work
License or certification needed: State journeyman electrician license and a valid driver's license
Pay range: $36 to $44 an hour
Hours and days: Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30, occasional Saturday by agreement
Benefits or extras: Shop truck, tool account, paid holidays
How to apply: Text a short note to 555-0117
What to include: License number, years of experience, and when you can start
Your name: Taylor Brooks
example.output:
Job title: Licensed residential electrician

Short intro: Bright Path Electric in Midway is hiring a licensed residential electrician for service calls, panel upgrades, and lighting work.

The work: Home service calls, panel upgrades, and lighting installs, Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30, with an occasional Saturday by agreement.

Who should apply: You have at least 4 years of residential work, a state journeyman electrician license, and a valid driver's license.

Pay and hours: $36 to $44 an hour.

Benefits: Shop truck, a tool account, and paid holidays.

How to apply: Text a short note to 555-0117 with your license number, years of experience, and when you can start.

Facts used: Bright Path Electric, Midway, $36 to $44 an hour, journeyman license.
Unknown: none.
example.notes: Made-up shop details, only to show a clear posting.
